- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–7 days.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; adjust upward by 1–2% for first 3 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift direction.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 5+ days, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- For 15–30 day forecasts, model often overestimates when sentiment is weak or mixed; apply 2–4% downward correction if sentiment <0.50 over last 7 days.
